title: Free ChatGPT has ads now. Here is what switching them off costs you. (v2 story map, 18 Nov)
experiment: Sensational covers and designed body type: the cover is a man in pyjamas recoiling from a chat assistant smothered in sponsored links, salesmen reaching out of the screen; each body card has a mono kicker, a mint rule and Archivo Black with the key phrase in mint.

five_whys.q: Why does a free ChatGPT user care?
five_whys.a: The free and Go plans now show a labelled ad under some answers, and the ads are on by default.

five_whys.q: Why are there ads at all?
five_whys.a: OpenAI says the free and Go plans need heavy infrastructure spending, and ads help fund wider access.

five_whys.q: Why do people not switch them off?
five_whys.a: The off switch sits in Settings, and no one explains what it takes away from you.

five_whys.q: Why is this wider than ChatGPT?
five_whys.a: Search and social media already run on ads, so free AI is following the same path.
Staff on free plans see ads beside work answers, so a team should pick its plan on purpose.

explains.temporary chat: a chat mode that shows no ads and does not save memories (card 7)

cards.headline: Free ChatGPT has ads now. Switching them off costs you.
cards.picture: Cover: a man in pyjamas recoiling from a chat assistant smothered in Sponsored cards, salesmen's arms reaching out of the screen
cards.line: Here is the price of each way out.

cards.headline: OpenAI now shows a labelled ad below some answers on the free and Go plans.
cards.picture: Real-looking answer screen with the Sponsored card circled, ChatGPT wordmark
cards.line: Ad testing began in the United States on 9 February 2026.

cards.headline: OpenAI says ads help pay for running the free and Go plans for hundreds of millions of people.
cards.picture: A free-plan ticket with a meter running behind it, ChatGPT wordmark

cards.headline: Free search and social media already run on ads, and free AI is now paying its way the same way.
cards.picture: Three doors labelled attention, money and features
cards.line: You pay with ads, money or limits.
cards.source: OpenAI, Our approach to advertising and expanding access to ChatGPT, 16 Jan 2026; Krish's research doc 'When the Assistant Becomes the Ad' (5 Nov 2026)

cards.headline: ChatGPT's eight dollar Go plan can still show ads, but the paid Plus and Pro plans show none.
cards.picture: Three price tags side by side: Go with an ad still on it, Plus and Pro clean
cards.line: Ad-free by payment starts at Plus.

cards.headline: In Settings, Ads controls lets free users go ad-free, at the cost of fewer daily messages and no image creation.
cards.picture: The settings path as three taps, then a crossed-out image tool and a short message meter
cards.line: Settings, Ads controls, Change plan to go ad-free.

cards.headline: ChatGPT's temporary chat mode shows no ads, and it does not create memories of what you say.
cards.picture: The trade-off scale: no ads on one side, no memory on the other

cards.headline: Choose your price on purpose: ads, money or limits, because every free answer costs you something.
cards.picture: The trade-off scale balanced, the house robot shrugging

facts_checked: help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt read live 18 Nov 2026: ads on Free and Go; none on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu; Ads-Free on Free = lower limits, no image generation or deep research; Temporary Chats show no ads; testing began 9 Feb 2026 in the US.
Go $8 and Plus $20 per month: CBS News and MacRumors, to confirm on chatgpt.com/pricing at the fact gate.

chatgpt.com/pricing read live 18 Nov 2026: Go $8 per month and 'may include ads'; Plus $20; Pro from $100. Help page: Temporary Chats show no ads and do not create or update memories. Cards 5 and 7 reworded after the cold read to match these; headlines changed since read_back.
